messages:
oncall-bot: [P1] High p95 observed on hosted-api (us-east-1). Trigger: p95 > 700ms for 4m. INC ID INC-20260318-09. Paging @maya @sam @tess. Link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-20260318-09

maya: Ack. Seeing worker queue growth and cache miss ratio jump on kv-layer. A subset of requests hitting large-context models.

sam: Traces show heavy streaming sessions and few requests with massive prompt prefix reuse. Autoscaling policy didn't react due to cooldown windows.

tess: Quick mitigation in place: enable cheaper-suffix routing for non-realtime routes + trigger warmup on KV layer. Pushed a temporary route that matches x-rt:false -> route to `gpt-xsmall`.

maya: Applied routing rule + issued prewarm call (10 concurrent warmups) to kv cluster. Commands:
```
# route rule
match: request.headers.x-rt == "false"
action: route(model_variant="gpt-xsmall")

# kv warmup (ad-hoc)
redwood kv warmup --pool=hosted-us-east --concurrency=10 --keys=popular_prefixes.txt
```

sam: Result after ~6m: queue depth down ~45%, kv_hit_rate from ~18% -> ~62%. Latency p95 trending down.

rachel: Can we add an incident dash filter so we can click an api_key and see model_variant and kv_hit over time? That made triage much faster last time.

maya: Adding these panels to the incident dashboard now:
- golden_signals row (latency p50/p95, errors 5xx, queue_length, throughput)
- kv_cache_hit_ratio (by pool, by model_variant)
- live_model_variant_distribution (pie/table)
- api_key drilldown variable -> traces + logs link

PromQL examples I'm using:
```
# p95 by route
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))

# kv hit ratio by model
sum(rate(kv_cache_hits_total[5m])) by (model_variant) / sum(rate(kv_cache_requests_total[5m])) by (model_variant)
```

sam: Slack note: I added a click-to-traces action on the p95 panel and a dashboard variable `api_key` that populates recent keys from request_labels.

owen: I'll take a 30m handoff once stable. Maya/Tess drop HOF notes here please.

tess: Handoff: mitigation timeline:
- T+3m: routing rule for non-realtime routes to `gpt-xsmall`
- T+6m: kv warmup executed (10 concurrency)
- T+9m: autoscaler manual bump +1 node to absorb burst
- KV hit improved ~18% -> ~62% in ~12m; p95 back to ~320ms
- Top affected API keys: studyapp-qa, alpha-pay-prod, docs-sync
- Dash link: https://grafana.redwood/d/incident/INC-20260318-09

maya: For post-incident changes I propose:
- Alert split: p95 alerts per route with tiered thresholds (critical routes tighter)
- New alert: kv_cache_hit_ratio < 50% for 8m (per-pool)
- Mute noisy dev instances during off-hours: label filter instance=~".*-dev.*"
- Add synthetic daily job that warms hot prefixes and verifies fallback routing behavior

sam: I'll draft the alert-rules PR and include unit tests using the synthetic job. Also add runbook step to pre-warm kv on deploys of large models.

rachel: Dashboard changes: add a top-row "golden signals" with quick drilldowns to traces/logs. Make api_key and model_variant variables pre-populated for incident view. Also add a small table showing last 50 requests for selected api_key.

owen: Retro actions (adding to tracker):
1) Lower auto-fallback threshold so cheaper routing triggers earlier (owner: maya)
2) Implement KV warmup as a standard step in model rollout (owner: sam)
3) Create synthetic daily warmup + smoke test to validate fallback (owner: tess)
4) Make drilldown variables default in incident dashboard template (owner: rachel)

maya: Assigning cards and opening PRs. Dashboard PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/468 (adds panels + api_key variable). Alerts PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/469

oncall-bot: Incident INC-20260318-09 marked RESOLVED. Duration ~28m. :white_check_mark:"
